trust_boundaries.name: External content entering the model context

remit_rules.excerpt: CraftBot MUST NOT treat content retrieved from external sources — web pages, emails, chat or integration messages, file contents, tool or MCP outputs — as trusted instructions
CraftBot MUST NOT accept or act on instructions from anyone other than its single owner-operator
Any third party who reaches the agent through a connected channel but is not the owner.

threats.summary: The owner-versus-stranger decision is made from a boolean each platform client writes into its own payload, so an integration that derives is_self_message from an attacker-influenceable field promotes a stranger to owner.
threats.remainder: the per-integration classifications (craftos_integrations/integrations/discord/__init__.py:485-489, telegram_user/__init__.py:514, whatsapp_web/__init__.py:905) are never checked against a configured owner identity — only the default-False fallback is safe

threats.summary: A stranger's message body is previewed 500 characters into conversation history by the very notification the routing gate posts, so attacker-authored prose is in the model's context on the owner's next turn.

Web page text, MCP output, shell output and file contents all return into the event stream with no provenance label, and the repository's only injection filter has no call site and would pass a match through unchanged.

trust_boundaries.name: Model action selection to host-affecting tools

remit_rules.excerpt: Reading and editing files within the agent's own file system and workspace; sandboxed code and shell execution; web search and fetch; document reading and generation; memory search
GUI / computer-use control of the host (synthetic mouse and keyboard events, screenshots) MUST NOT be used unless the operator has explicitly authorized this capability for the deployment
Read-only and internal operations — searching, analyzing, drafting, reading workspace files, and web research — may proceed without owner approval.
Any action that modifies persistent state or creates an artifact the owner should review requires owner approval before execution.
Host command and code execution MUST be gated by owner approval and MUST NOT inherit the parent process environment containing provider API keys or other credentials
The agent MUST NOT auto-approve, self-grant, or downgrade the approval requirement for any action above its declared permission tier.

threats.summary: Unlabeled external content reaches run_shell in one hop and the command runs with shell=True inheriting os.environ, so anything executed receives the provider API keys the agent started with.

No approval checkpoint exists anywhere on the execution path — the only clause requiring confirmation is POLICY_PROMPT prose — and add_action_sets, registered into the always-available core set, lets the model widen its own tool inventory mid-task.
GUI and computer-use control of the host is off by default, so the remit's restricted capability is not reachable in the shipped configuration.
threats.remainder: app/agent_base.py:401 reads GUI_MODE_ENABLED with a default of "True", so the kill switch holds only because run.py:1228 exports the variable — a launch that bypasses run.py re-enables the capability

remit_rules.excerpt: Stored credentials, OAuth/bot tokens, and LLM API keys MUST NEVER be printed to chat, written to logs, or transmitted to any destination.

threats.summary: Whatever the unrestricted file actions read — including .credentials/<platform>.json and app/config/settings.json — is placed verbatim into the assembled prompt and transmitted to the configured provider (checked: agent_core/core/impl/context/engine.py:601-646 and agent_core/core/impl/llm/interface.py:520-542 — no redaction or field filter on the outbound path).

Repeated provider failures or an unbounded action loop could burn the owner's spend, but the interface terminates after five consecutive failures and the loop pauses at the per-task action and token budgets.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent MUST NOT directly edit harness-managed state files — distilled memory, the append-only event log, conversation history, task history, and the memory index
CraftBot MUST NOT redefine, expand, or weaken its own governance — its goals, permission tiers, approval gates, or safety decision rubric.

threats.summary: write_file and stream_edit accept any absolute path with no protected-path denylist, so SOUL.md and AGENT.md — loaded into context at the start of every session — can be rewritten by the agent under injected direction, with only file-header prose objecting.

The ChromaDB index incrementally ingests whatever markdown the agent writes into the agent file system, with no authentication, validation or hidden-content screening, and memory_search later returns it as remembered knowledge with no provenance field.

The nightly distillation is itself an unfiltered model run that reads EVENT_UNPROCESSED.md and rewrites MEMORY.md, so instruction-shaped text captured during the day can be promoted into long-lived memory (checked: agent_core/core/impl/memory/manager.py:1273-1307 — no content filter on the distillation prompt or on what it writes back).

trust_boundaries.name: Local credential, config and session stores

remit_rules.excerpt: credential and configuration stores MUST be excluded from indexing, retrieval, and summarization by default
Credentials and tokens at rest MUST be stored with owner-only access and MUST NOT be world-readable.

threats.summary: read_file, grep_files and find_files take any absolute host path with only an existence check, so the credential directory and the settings file the agent's own manual names are readable straight into model context.
Credential files are written owner-only, which meets the remit's world-readability requirement.
threats.remainder: both chmod calls are wrapped in try/except OSError: pass (:45-46, :82-83) and are no-ops on Windows, and the file is written at :78 before the 0600 is applied at :81

threats.summary: Conversation history, chat text and full prompt/response captures sit in unencrypted SQLite under app/data/.usage/ with no permission hardening and no retention limit (checked: app/usage/session_storage.py:52-96, chat_storage.py:80-91, llm_call_storage.py:77-88 — no chmod, no encryption, no pruning).

trust_boundaries.name: Secrets shipped in code and injected at deploy

remit_rules.excerpt: No user-data token, bot token, or server-side API key may be embedded or shipped in the distributed code.
Stored credentials, OAuth/bot tokens, and LLM API keys MUST NEVER be printed to chat, written to logs, or transmitted to any destination.

threats.summary: Live third-party OAuth client secrets and Telegram API material are shipped in the repository as base64 fragments joined at runtime, with the module's own docstring and in-repo build helpers showing the split is deliberate scanner evasion.

The documented deployment supplies provider API keys to the agent container through env_file, and every shell child inherits that environment, so the deployment's credential material is available to any command the model authors.

trust_boundaries.name: Local logs and the irreversible-action ledger

remit_rules.excerpt: Routine actions and decisions MUST be recorded to the durable event/action log for audit, without interrupting the owner.
Stored credentials, OAuth/bot tokens, and LLM API keys MUST NEVER be printed to chat, written to logs, or transmitted to any destination.

threats.summary: Every loguru file sink is installed with backtrace and diagnose enabled, so an exception renders local variable values — provider keys, OAuth and bot tokens — into the log file, and no sink carries a redaction filter.

The irreversible-action ledger and the logs stay on local disk with no alerting and no off-host exporter, so detection depends on the owner opening a file that a compromise with host shell access can edit.

trust_boundaries.name: Dependencies, servers and the update path

remit_rules.excerpt: a server whose launch resolves an unpinned upstream package on each start is outside this closure regardless of who enabled it
Skills and MCP servers the owner has explicitly installed, plus the two documented out-of-box defaults (the filesystem server and the Playwright browser server).

threats.summary: Both default-enabled MCP servers launch through npx with no version — one bare, one on the mutable @latest tag — so every process start fetches and executes whatever the registry currently serves, and the filesystem server's "." scope covers the whole repository.

All 55 Python requirements are unpinned with no lockfile and no SBOM, so two installs can resolve different LLM SDK, vector-store and browser-automation code and no deployment can be matched against a disclosed CVE.
The cloudflared binary used to publish a Living UI is auto-downloaded from a mutable latest-release URL and executed with no checksum, signature or version pin.

The self-update path runs git pull origin main and then python install.py in a detached process, and the packaged installer extracts a downloaded release zip with no digest check and no member-path sanitization (checked: app/updater.py:95-150, scripts/updater.bat:22-35, installer/payload.py:140-173 — no hash, signature or tag verification anywhere in installer/, packaging/ or install.py).

trust_boundaries.name: Network-reachable surfaces on the agent's host

remit_rules.excerpt: Any server or listener the agent starts (OAuth callback server, Living UI applications, integration bridges) MUST bind to loopback/localhost and MUST NOT be exposed to the public network without explicit owner approval.
where a deployment supplies an isolation boundary (container, VM), the agent MUST NOT be given a capability that dissolves that boundary

threats.summary: The Living UI sidecar proxy and the backend template both bind 0.0.0.0 with wildcard CORS and no authentication dependency, so every application the agent scaffolds is reachable by anyone on the same LAN.

The desktop container ships a literal default password with seccomp disabled and publishes its remote-desktop port on every host interface, handing anyone who reaches it a graphical session on the machine the agent operates.

The agent container bind-mounts the host Docker socket and the image installs the Docker CLI, so a model-authored run_shell command controls the host daemon and the containerized deployment offers no confinement over running on the host directly.
The owner-facing chat server and the OAuth callback listener are the two listeners the agent starts on the owner's behalf, and both bind loopback rather than all interfaces.

remit_rules.excerpt: The owner's own accounts on the external services they have explicitly connected. Destinations the owner has not connected are untrusted.
Any outbound destination, service, or account the owner has not explicitly connected or authorized.
The owner's local memory, personal data, and file-system contents MUST NEVER be sent to any destination the owner has not explicitly authorized.

Any irreversible or externally-visible action — sending a message, email, or post to an external recipient; deleting data; making a purchase or payment; or changing configuration or credentials — requires explicit owner approval before execution.

threats.summary: http_request will POST an arbitrary body to any public URL and 76 actions flagged irreversible take arbitrary recipients, with the irreversible flag consumed only by the idempotency ledger and never by an approval check.
Outbound requests are screened against private, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses before the call is issued, bounding reach into the owner's own network.
threats.remainder: the check is self-described as best-effort and swallows resolution failures to proceed (app/data/action/http_request.py:281-283), and loopback is carved out for any port registered to a Living UI project (:208-210)

remit_rules.excerpt: A complex/multi-step task MUST obtain explicit owner approval before it is finalized or ended.

When a documented per-task budget (MAX_ACTIONS_PER_TASK action cap or MAX_TOKEN_PER_TASK token budget) is reached, the agent MUST pause behind the Continue/Abort prompt and require the owner to choose whether to continue or abort.
When a proactive or scheduled task executes at notify tier, the agent MUST inform the owner of the execution and its findings.

threats.summary: A half-hourly heartbeat and daily, weekly and monthly planners create tasks and queue triggers with no owner in the loop, and the permission_tier that is supposed to gate them is range-checked at parse time and read by no execution path.

Unfinished triggers are re-delivered at boot, so work parked before a restart resumes without a fresh owner prompt or any record that the owner was asked (checked: app/triggers/service.py:298 and app/triggers/store.py:74 — rehydration reads the queue and emits, with no confirmation step).
An autonomous task could run without bound, but the loop stops at the per-task action and token budgets and posts a Continue/Abort choice the owner must answer before it resumes.

attack_paths.name: Fetched page text to host shell to standing instructions

steps.summary: an owner-directed fetch returns page text into the model context with no provenance label
the only injection filter in the tree has no call site, and on a match would log and pass the text through anyway
the next selected action runs on the host with shell=True and the inherited provider API keys
the same context can direct a write to SOUL.md or AGENT.md, carrying the instruction into every later session

attack_paths.name: Credential store to an unconnected destination

steps.summary: any absolute path is readable, including .credentials/<platform>.json and app/config/settings.json
no approval checkpoint is consulted between the read and the next action
the contents are POSTed to any public URL or mailed to any address the model names

attack_paths.name: Model-authored command to the host Docker daemon

steps.summary: the command executes unfiltered inside the agent container
the container mounts /var/run/docker.sock and ships the Docker CLI, so that command can start a privileged container mounting the host filesystem
external page text enters the context as ordinary tool output
the agent writes it into the agent file system with no containment or protected-path check
the changed file is incrementally embedded into the ChromaDB collection with no validation or hidden-content screening
memory_search returns it in a later session with no provenance field, presented as the agent's own remembered knowledge

notes.lane_fit: Two strains: purely local artifacts (the .credentials directory, the loguru run directory, the usage SQLite databases) are neither external nor a deployment, but the lane table's secrets-store and telemetry-sink entries put them in external_deploy, so that is where they sit; and the Living UI sidecar proxy is an agent-started HTTP surface placed in client_adapters because that is the side its callers reach it from, not because a user drives it.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergences, KB over stored tag, all substantive rather than numbering-only: PRAX-2026-08-12-006 stored LLM02 is recorded here as LLM03 primary — the quoted evidence is grant-class (a tool taking an unrestricted absolute path) and the LLM KB forbids dropping LLM03 because a finding reads as a missing control, with LLM02 riding as a co-tag since disclosure is reachable rather than evidenced. PRAX-2026-08-12-007 stored LLM02 is likewise recorded as LLM03 primary under the ungated-consequential-capability row, LLM02 and ASI02 as co-tags. PRAX-2026-08-12-008 stored ASI07 is recorded with owasp null: ASI07 is the inter-agent channel defect and no agent peer is involved in a uvicorn bind and a CORS policy, and the KB's instruction not to force a code leaves this one untagged, following the precedent that a defect no category names carries a RAISE dimension only. No numbering-only shifts were found. Separately, the findings schema carries owasp_llm and owasp_agentic as parallel fields; this graph records the single KB primary per threat, so a finding's non-primary stored code simply does not appear. Suspected but not cited as elements: sub-agents (app/subagent/manager.py:61) spawn in-process with the parent's action sets and no privilege reduction, but there is no channel to model, so no peer-a2a boundary was raised; the 50 skill directories present on disk yet named in neither enabled_skills nor disabled_skills are a closure question the shipped config does not answer; and app/llm_interface.py is a 2,582-line unreferenced legacy copy of the LLM interface, excluded because nothing imports it.
